issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision preserving and deeming prior acts under a successor law applies to judicial orders as well as administrative acts.
material_facts: A custodian had made an order adjudicating a claim to property and releasing it.
A later law preserved prior acts and treated them as acts under the successor law, and a superior custodian relied on that provision to revise the order.
issues.conclusion: The deeming provision was not confined to administrative acts; it also applied to judicial orders.
issues.legal_principle: Section 58(3) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 applies to judicial orders as well as administrative acts. Indira Sohan Lal v. Custodian of Evacuee Property, Delhi, was followed on this point.

predicates.appeal_challenges_revision_of_prior_prop: A party appealed an authority's decision to revise an earlier order concerning property.
predicates.prior_custodian_order_was_judicial: A custodian decided a claim affecting property rights by making an order.
predicates.successor_law_deems_prior_actions_contin: A later law treated acts done under an earlier law as acts under the later law.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges revision of a prior property order that was judicial and a successor law deems prior actions continued, the deeming provision applies to the judicial order.

issues.legal_issue: An order made by a custodian that is not covered by an intervening law's limited deeming provision does not pass through a chain of legislative fictions into later laws.
material_facts: The original order releasing the property was made by a custodian under an earlier ordinance, not by a claims officer.
An intervening ordinance deemed only orders made by claims officers to have been made under that ordinance, and only for appeal or revision purposes.
The superior custodian later treated the original order as an order made under the later law.
issues.conclusion: The original order was not deemed to have been made under the successive ordinances and the Act, so it could not be revised on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(7) of Ordinance XIII of 2006 carried forward only orders made by a Claims Officer under the earlier ordinance, and only for appeal or revision. Because the original order was made by the Custodian, that limited deeming provision did not apply; consequently, the later deeming provisions could not carry the order forward as an order made under the Act.

predicates.revision_under_later_property_law: An authority sought to revise an order under a later law governing property administration.
predicates.original_order_made_by_custodian_not_cla: A custodian, rather than a claims officer, made the original order.
predicates.intervening_deeming_rule_covers_only_cla: An intervening law carried forward only orders made by claims officers.

issues.definition: When a later-law revision concerns an order made by a custodian and the intervening deeming rule covers only claims-officer orders, the original order is not deemed made under the later law.

issues.legal_issue: A successor law's deeming provision does not deprive an order of finality that it acquired under the earlier law before the successor law came into force.
material_facts: The order had become final under the earlier ordinance because no appeal was filed against it.
The Act came into force after the order had become final.
The Act preserved the previous operation of the repealed law and deemed certain earlier acts to have been done under the Act.
The superior custodian later used the Act's revision power to set aside the order.
issues.conclusion: The Act could not retrospectively deprive the order of its acquired finality, and the superior custodian could not revise it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 25 and 28 of Ordinance XXVII of 1949 made the unappealed order final. Section 58(3) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 preserved the previous operation of the repealed law, and its deeming provision did not unsettle that finality. The Court applied Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving and Delhi Cloth and General Mills v. Income-tax Commissioner, Delhi, and distinguished Indira Sohan Lal because the order there was made while the proceeding was still pending.

predicates.revision_under_successor_property_law: An authority sought to revise an earlier order under a successor law governing property administration.
predicates.prior_order_became_final_under_earlier_l: An earlier order became final under the law then in force before the successor law took effect.
predicates.successor_law_preserves_prior_operation: The successor law preserved the earlier law's previous operation while deeming certain prior actions to have been taken under the successor law.

issues.definition: When a revision under a successor property law concerns an order already final under the earlier law, and the successor law preserves the earlier law's prior operation, the final order cannot be reopened.

issues.legal_issue: The successor law's revision power over orders of any custodian at any time is limited to orders within the successor law's scope that had not become final before it came into force.
material_facts: The Act enlarged the superior custodian's revision power compared with the repealed ordinance.
The order at issue had become final under the repealed ordinance before the Act came into force.
The superior custodian relied on the Act's references to orders of any custodian and revision at any time.
issues.conclusion: Those expressions cover orders of custodians defined under the Act and orders deemed made under it that had not become final before it came into force; they do not authorize revision of an order already final under the earlier law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 must be read subject to section 58(3). The words “any time” and “any Custodian” do not confer retrospective power to disturb final orders; they cover orders of custodians under the Act and orders deemed to have been made under it that were not final when the Act came into force.

predicates.revision_under_successor_property_law: An authority sought to revise an order under a successor law governing property administration.
predicates.order_within_successor_law_scope: The order was made by an officer covered by the successor law or was deemed made under that law.
predicates.order_not_final_when_successor_law_began: The order had not become final under the earlier law when the successor law took effect.

issues.definition: When a revision under a successor property law concerns an order within that law's scope that was not yet final when the law began, the successor revision power covers the order.
